requirement:
The Rust outline profile under {cite}`requirements.references.outlines` MUST
identify items by segments describing their syntactic ancestry within the file,
such as `fn[run]`, `struct[Packet]`, and `mod[local]/fn[run]`, and MUST NOT
resolve Rust modules across files. Functions, methods, structs, enums, unions,
traits, impls, modules, macros, constants, statics, type aliases, and extern
blocks MUST be outline nodes. Impl segments MUST be named by their syntactic self
type and optional trait path, as `impl[Thing]` and `impl[Thing/Trait]`. `use`
declarations and other items without a suitable name MUST be anonymous. Selector
spelling MUST be documented.
rationale:
The reviewed tests cover each obligation in `requirements.references.rust_item_selectors`. I did not read the implementation source. I judged the tests against the requirement text.

- **Selectors by syntactic ancestry.**
  - `rust_selectors_follow_syntactic_ancestry` asserts `mod[local]/fn[run]`, `fn[outer]/fn[inner]`, `trait[Trait]/fn[read]`, `extern[C]/fn[puts]` and `impl[Thing]/fn[run]`. It also resolves each selector back to the same node.
  - `selectors_name_syntactic_ancestry_and_duplicates` repeats most of these.
  - `rust_items_attach_documentation_and_preserve_structural_hashes` in `tests/outline_content.rs` asserts the full selector list `mod[auth]`, `mod[auth]/fn[check]`, `mod[auth]/struct[Token]`, `fn[last]`. It also checks kinds and spans.
- **No resolution of modules across files.** `functions_in_a_separate_module_file_are_selected_within_that_file` outlines `lib.rs` containing `mod local;` and a separate `local.rs`. It asserts the second file yields only `fn[run]`, with no `mod[local]` segment.
- **Required node kinds.** `rust_selectors_follow_syntactic_ancestry` asserts these selectors:
  - functions: `fn[...]`
  - methods: `impl[..]/fn[run]`
  - structs: `struct[Thing]`
  - enums: `enum[E]`
  - unions: `union[U]`
  - traits: `trait[Trait]`
  - impls
  - modules: `mod[...]`
  - macros: `macro[make]`
  - constants: `const[C]`
  - statics: `static[S]`
  - type aliases: `type[Alias]`
  - extern blocks: `extern[C]` and `extern[Rust]`
- **Impl naming.**
  - `impl[Thing]` and `impl[Thing/Trait]` are asserted in the selector tests.
  - Generic self types are covered by `impl[Wrapper<T>/Trait]` in `item_macros_are_anonymous_nodes_and_expression_macros_are_not`.
  - A path-qualified trait is covered by `impl[Thing/core::fmt::Display]` in the `outline_content.rs` test.
  - A non-path self type is covered by `impl[%5Bu8;%204%5D]`.
- **Anonymous nodes.**
  - `use` declarations get distinct `use@...` selectors, asserted in `selectors_name_syntactic_ancestry_and_duplicates`.
  - Item-position macro invocations get `macro@<12 hex>` selectors, asserted by regex and distinctness in `item_macros_are_anonymous_nodes_and_expression_macros_are_not`.
  - The same test asserts that macro invocations inside function bodies are not nodes, by checking the selector count.
- **Selector spelling documented.** `every_profile_mapping_is_documented` checks that `md/reference.md` contains each example selector. These include `mod[local]/fn[run]`, `impl[Thing/Trait]/fn[run]`, `extern[C]/fn[puts]`, `impl[Wrapper<T>/Trait]` and `use@3f2a9c01b7de`. It also checks the anonymity sentence and "Modules are never resolved across files.", and that every profile kind and extension is in the table.

I found no obligation without a test, and no assertion that contradicts the requirement.

text: :::{req} rust_item_selectors
The Rust outline profile under {cite}`requirements.references.outlines` MUST
identify items by segments describing their syntactic ancestry within the file,
such as `fn[run]`, `struct[Packet]`, and `mod[local]/fn[run]`, and MUST NOT
resolve Rust modules across files. Functions, methods, structs, enums, unions,
traits, impls, modules, macros, constants, statics, type aliases, and extern
blocks MUST be outline nodes. Impl segments MUST be named by their syntactic self
type and optional trait path, as `impl[Thing]` and `impl[Thing/Trait]`. `use`
declarations and other items without a suitable name MUST be anonymous. Selector
spelling MUST be documented.
:::{req} outlines
Habeas MUST parse Rust, Python, TypeScript, CSS, Markdown, TOML, and YAML
sources with pinned tree-sitter grammars, selected by file extension compared
case-insensitively. When validating outline evidence inputs, Habeas MUST report
the line of the first syntax error in a recovered outline. Every
other text file MUST use a plain-text profile in which each line that is not
blank is an anonymous outline node of kind `line`. Each supported language MUST
have an outline profile that maps grammar node kinds to short outline kind names
and, for each mapped kind, states whether a node is named, and by which fields
or children, or anonymous. Only mapped kinds MUST appear in the outline, except
that a Markdown profile MAY additionally recognize colon-fenced directive
containers under {cite}`requirements.sdk.sources.markdown.fence_precedence`
and expose them as outline nodes under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.sources.markdown.fenced_blocks`. Such containers MUST
preserve source ranges and containment, and MUST NOT be recognized within
literal code or raw HTML. Other nodes MUST be transparent, so their outline
descendants appear under the nearest outline ancestor. A profile MAY attach grammar siblings to an outline
node, such as Rust attributes and doc comments preceding an item, so the outline
tree need not match the grammar tree exactly; attached siblings are part of that
node for its line range and hash. Every file's outline MUST have a root node
for the whole file, independent of language. Source in no other outline node,
such as top-level statements no profile maps, MUST belong to the root node;
profiles MUST NOT invent fallback kinds for it. Comments MUST NOT be outline nodes. Profiles MUST be
documented. Upgrading a grammar or profile MAY change outlines and MUST be
treated as a deliberate change.
